overview: Nauru is a tiny island country in the central Pacific and the smallest republic in the world. It has no official capital; government offices are in the district of Yaren. Nauru became independent in 1968. It grew rich from mining phosphate, but most of the phosphate has now been dug up.

geography.text: Nauru is a single raised coral island, ringed by a reef and a narrow coastal strip where most people live. The central plateau, called Topside, was mined for phosphate for decades, leaving a landscape of jagged limestone pinnacles where little can grow.

history.text: Nauru was settled by Micronesian and Polynesian peoples. It became a German colony in 1888, and phosphate mining began in 1906. After the First World War it was run jointly by Australia, Britain and New Zealand. Nauru became independent in 1968 and for a time was one of the richest countries in the world per person, until the phosphate began to run out.

events.title: Japanese occupation
events.text: Japan occupies the island; many Nauruans are deported.

government.text: Nauru is a parliamentary republic with no political parties in the usual sense. Its 19-member parliament elects the President, who is both head of state and head of government. Nauru has no official capital; government offices are in Yaren.

economy.text: Phosphate mining once made Nauru one of the richest countries in the world per person, but the deposits are now mostly used up and much of the island is a stripped landscape. An offshore detention centre run for Australia has been a major source of income.

culture.text: Nauru is the third-smallest country in the world and the smallest island country. It is a single raised coral island just 21 km² in area. The national language is Nauruan, though English is widely used.

items.title: Topside
items.text: The mined-out plateau that covers most of the island.

items.title: Angam Day
items.text: Celebrates the times Nauru's population recovered to 1,500.

sport.text: Australian rules football is the national sport, and weightlifting has brought Nauru Commonwealth Games medals.

items.title: Marcus Stephen
items.text: Weightlifting champion who later became President.

didYouKnow: Nauru is the smallest island country in the world, at about 21 km².
Nauru has no official capital city.

keyPeople.name: Marcus Stephen
keyPeople.text: Won Commonwealth gold before becoming President.
